controls.label: Shape
controls.qualification: A sphere of the published radius, lit by Orkaria; the neutral gray is a display convention, not a measured color.
controls.notes: No image or color of GJ 1214 b is published: the sphere has its measured size, and the gray marks an unresolved surface. The lighting is its own star's, at the measured orbit. The gray takes the color of gj-1214's light, as its color dataset measures it.

controls.label: JWST
controls.qualification: Published fit · Kempton et al. (2023) · a JWST MIRI 5–12 µm phase curve of 20–22 July 2022 · longitude only
controls.notes: Brightness temperature across 5–12 µm of GJ 1214 b from Kempton et al. (2023)'s published fit to a JWST MIRI 5–12 µm phase curve of 20–22 July 2022. Their Fourier series becomes a map of longitude through the Cowan & Agol (2008) inversion, so there is no north-south detail and every latitude is drawn alike. The hottest longitude is 20° east of noon. Longitudes where the fit gives no emission are left blank. The false color runs from 150 to 650 K. With shadows on, the star's light darkens the night half.

charts.alt: The orbits of Orkaria's planets in this map from above, to scale, with GJ 1214 b highlighted and the direction to Earth down. Each orbit is the one the app draws, from the published period, a/R*, eccentricity and argument of periastron; the star is a marker, not to scale.

GJ 1214 b's transmission spectrum: the fraction of starlight the planet blocks as it crosses its star, larger where its atmosphere absorbs. 22 measured bins from Kreidberg et al. 2014 (Hubble Space Telescope satellite, Wide Field Camera 3), as the NASA Exoplanet Archive lists them. Horizontal bars are wavelength bins; vertical bars are the published 1-sigma errors.

GJ 1214 b's dayside emission: the light lost as the planet passes behind its star: its day side's own glow and reflected light. 14 measured bins from Kempton et al. 2023 (NASA 6.5m James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Satellite Mission, Mid-Infrared Instrument (MIRI) - LRS), as the NASA Exoplanet Archive lists them. Horizontal bars are wavelength bins; vertical bars are the published 1-sigma errors.
